title: ILO Declaration on Fundamental Principles and Rights at Work — applied to AI data-labelling supply chains
description: General international core labour standards, applied here to the AI data-labelling/content-moderation supply chain in the absence of any dedicated AI-specific labour framework. This absence is itself a notable governance gap: as of this record, no framework equivalent to NIST AI RMF or the EU AI Act exists specifically for AI supply-chain labour conditions. 'Community' confidence reflects both the general (not AI-specific) nature of the source and the fact this is a general framework applied to a novel context, not a verbatim-quoted provision.
framework_name: ILO Declaration on Fundamental Principles and Rights at Work
control_reference: Core principles (freedom of association, elimination of forced/child labour, elimination of discrimination, and — per the 2022 addition — a safe and healthy working environment)
control_text: Applied to AI data-labelling supply chains: workers engaged (directly or via a vendor) to perform psychologically demanding content-review work are entitled to a safe and healthy working environment, which in this context implies documented exposure limits, fair compensation, and access to psychological support — general labour principles applied to a context no AI-specific labour framework yet directly governs.

relationships.reason: Satisfying this control requires an observable, independently-conducted welfare audit.
